title: The pseudo-quantum representation of finite reversible Markov chains
abstract: The pseudo-quantum representation re-encodes a finite, irreducible, reversible continuous-time Markov chain with $M$ states as a complex-orthogonal flow on a doubled space of dimension $2M$. After uniformisation, a square-root gauge, a doubling of the state space and a diagonal unitary twist, the chain generates an entire one-parameter group $W_z = e^{zK}$ with $z$ complex, and this single group is the object of the paper. Its real slice, $z$ real, reproduces the stochastic semigroup exactly through an explicit decoding whose probabilistic meaning is the parity of the number of ticks of the uniformised chain. Its imaginary slice, $z = iθ$, is a finite-dimensional unitary quantum system. The chain and the quantum system are therefore not two analogous models but two restrictions of one entire representation. The setup also produces, with no further input, a pseudo-Schroedinger equation, a bilinear von Neumann equation for a complex-symmetric pseudo-density, and a pseudo-Bloch vector equation on a non-compact quadric. We develop the construction from first principles and work out one model completely, the usual symmetric Ehrenfest urn. Its gauged generator equals $(2/n) J_x$, the spin-$n/2$ operator, its relaxation modes are Lorentz boosts, and its imaginary slice is a depth-one quantum circuit whose Born distribution is the classical urn law under the clock $θ(t) = \arccos(e^{-2t})$. The same clock identifies the Fisher-Rao lift of the urn trajectory with a rigid spin-coherent-state orbit. This is a preliminary simplified version of a longer paper. It treats only finite state spaces and only the symmetric Ehrenfest urn, and it previews without proofs the asymmetric urn, two queues, the symmetric simple exclusion process and the stochastic Ising model. Appendix primers make the quantum, geometric and information-theoretic language self-contained.
summary: The paper introduces the pseudo-quantum representation (PQR) to unify Markov chain dynamics and quantum evolution into one framework. It shows that both classical dissipation and unitary quantum mechanics emerge as specific restrictions of this single, complex-valued mathematical object. This provides a deep structural connection between statistical physics and quantum theory.
main_problem: The paper aims to unify two seemingly distinct descriptions of dynamics—dissipative Markov chain evolution and unitary quantum evolution—by showing they both arise as restrictions of a single mathematical object: the pseudo-quantum representation (PQR).
main_result: The PQR generates an entire one-parameter group $Wz$, where its real slice ($z$ real) reproduces the classical Markov semigroup, and its imaginary slice ($z=i	heta$) yields a genuine unitary quantum evolution.
method: The core method involves constructing the PQR using complex-orthogonal flows on a doubled state space, utilizing a bilinear pairing to achieve holomorphy in complex time $z$.
model_or_system: The primary model is a finite, irreducible, reversible continuous-time Markov chain. The paper develops this framework by analyzing the symmetric Ehrenfest urn as a detailed example.
key_observables: Pseudo-density $ho_z$, pseudo-wave $\Phi_z$, Bloch vector $r$, and various divergence measures like KL divergence and Fisher–Rao distance.
important_parameters: The complex time parameter $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the Markov chain generator $Q$, and the clock angle $	heta(t) = \arccos(e^{-2t})$ for the Ehrenfest case.
main_assumptions: The analysis is preliminary, focusing only on finite state spaces and the symmetric Ehrenfest urn; it also assumes standard results from Lie theory and information geometry.
paper_structure: The paper builds the PQR framework by defining the complex flow $Wz$, then analyzing its real slice (Markov dynamics) and imaginary slice (Quantum dynamics). It develops this using specific examples like the Ehrenfest urn, linking it to spin algebra, Lorentz boosts, and quantum circuits.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mathematical bridge between classical stochastic processes and unitary quantum mechanics, suggesting that many physical systems are governed by a single underlying complex structure. This is highly relevant for open quantum systems theory.
